title: Living As If God Isn't There
overview: This psalm, an almost word-for-word repeat of Psalm 14, describes people who act as if God doesn't matter, how they treat others, and a longing for God to rescue his people.

parts.label: The fool's claim (v. 1)
parts.note: In Hebrew, a "fool" isn't someone with low intelligence but someone morally reckless, who lives as though no God will ever hold them to account. The psalm links that inner attitude directly to corrupt, harmful behavior.

parts.label: God looks down (vv. 2-3)
parts.note: The poet pictures God searching humanity for anyone who truly understands and seeks him, and finding no one who does good. Christians later read this through Paul, who quotes these lines in his letter to the Romans to argue that every person needs God's rescue.

parts.label: Eating up my people (v. 4)
parts.note: The wrongdoers consume vulnerable people as casually as they eat a meal, and they never pray or turn to God. "My people" likely means the faithful or oppressed within Israel, though it could also voice God's own view of them.

parts.label: Sudden terror (v. 5)
parts.note: The attackers are seized by panic where there seemed nothing to fear, and their bones are left scattered, which in that culture meant the deep disgrace of lying unburied. This verse differs from Psalm 14 and may have been reworded to recall a particular military rescue, though scholars are unsure which one.

parts.label: Longing for rescue (v. 6)
parts.note: Zion is the hill in Jerusalem where the temple stood, so the poet hopes God's help will come from his dwelling place. "Restores his people" can mean bringing them back from exile or simply restoring their fortunes, and Jacob and Israel are two names for the same nation.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether "there is no one who does good" describes every human being without exception, as Paul's use of it suggests, or mainly the oppressors in the psalm, set against the faithful "people" they harm.
think: When people treat others carelessly or cruelly, do you think it comes more from what they believe, or from what they think they can get away with?
